tools.name: omni_video_generation
tools.description: Generates video (with optional embedded audio) from a text prompt, optionally conditioned on input images and/or videos, using Google's Gemini Omni model via the Vertex Interactions API. Returns MP4(s) saved locally and/or to GCS.

prompt.description: The text prompt describing the video to generate.

model.description:
The Gemini Omni model ID to use for video generation. Supported models:
- gemini-omni-1.1-flash-preview (Aliases: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, Omni 1.1, Omni) - Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash (Preview): text/image/video in, text+video out, via the Vertex Interactions API (global only). Supports 360p/720p/1080p/4k video output.
- gemini-omni-flash-preview (Aliases: Gemini Omni Flash) - Gemini Omni Flash (Preview): text/image/video in, text+video out, via the Vertex Interactions API (global only).

images.description: Optional. Up to 10 input images to condition generation on. Each entry is a local file path or a gs:// URI (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp).

videos.description: Optional. Input videos to reference or edit. Each entry is a local file path or a gs:// URI (e.g. video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime).

sample_count.description: Optional. Number of videos to generate (1-3, default 1). Clamped to the model maximum of 3.

temperature.description: Optional. Sampling temperature, 0.0-2.0 (higher = more varied). Sent in generation_config.

top_p.description: Optional. Nucleus sampling probability mass, 0.0-1.0. Sent in generation_config.

output_directory.description: Optional. Local directory to save the generated video(s) to.

gcs_bucket_uri.description: Optional. GCS URI prefix to store generated video(s) (e.g., your-bucket/outputs/). Falls back to GENMEDIA_BUCKET+/omni_outputs/ if set.

output_filename.description: Optional. Client-predictable base name for the generated file(s). The extension is forced to the true output media type (e.g. .mp4). When a single video is produced the name is used as-is (e.g. 'clip.mp4'); when multiple videos are produced they are suffixed '_1', '_2', ... before the extension (e.g. 'clip_1.mp4'). An existing file/object of the same name is overwritten.
